html: The Ka:'yu:'k't'h' (Kyuquot) and Che:k'tles7et'h' (Checleseht) are two Nuu-chah-nulth peoples of the north-west coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia, around Kyuquot Sound and Checleset Bay. They now form one First Nation. They lived from the sea, hunting seals, sea otters and whales and fishing salmon and halibut, and in the late 1700s took part in the sea otter fur trade with British and American ships. Their main village is Houpsitas, reached by boat or floatplane. They signed the Maa-nulth Treaty with Canada and British Columbia, which took effect in 2011. Their southern kin include the Tseshaht.
